public_comment.topic: Asked whether the easement/deed restricting structures at the Hickory Hills pumping station is a recorded legal document, and whether Hickory Hills residents had sent any letter committing to remove kayaks/canoes stored there.

votes.motion: Rescind the prior (June 10th) vote that had cancelled/changed the plan to switch billing software, and continue moving forward with the vendor (referred to as the 'beta' company)
Approve the pipe quote from EJP (EJ Prescott) for the Metal Lane water main replacement project
Approve purchase of $14,557.89 of materials (excluding hydrants) from Ferguson for the Metal Lane water main replacement project, funded from the equipment and main account
Approve $7,300 for the purchase of two hydrants for the Metal Lane main from the hydrant vendor (heard as 'FW')

budget_items.what_was_said: After an additional meeting with the vendor, the board decided to proceed with switching accounting systems effective July 1 to align with the new fiscal year, while the actual resident-billing switch may slip to October 1st or January 1st depending on testing.
Ductile iron pipe pricing was compared to the lowest PVC bid; PVC was chosen as a test run for the Metal Lane project, with the pipe quote awarded to EJP.
Ferguson won the materials quote; removing the hydrants from that quote brought the material cost down, to be paid from the equipment and main account.
Two hydrants were purchased separately from the materials quote to match the M&H brand already used on the rest of the project.

Using PVC instead of ductile iron was said to save enough per street that two streets could be done for the cost of one; a prior project (Rolling Acres) was said to have saved roughly half a million dollars by doing the work in-house.

budget_items.topic: Hydrant maintenance reimbursement from the town
budget_items.what_was_said: The district receives a flat annual reimbursement from the town's fire department budget for hydrant maintenance, unchanged by the number of hydrants; a commissioner raised whether hydrant testing/flushing costs are fully covered and asked it be revisited.

budget_items.topic: Cost and revenue from bulk/commercial water sales
budget_items.what_was_said: The district calculated its cost to pump/treat water per million gallons versus what it charges bulk buyers (mainly one large commercial hauler), estimating roughly the stated annual revenue since sales began, which offsets what would otherwise be charged to the roughly 2,500 users.

budget_items.topic: PFAS/PAS water treatment and SRF funding
budget_items.what_was_said: Voters denied SRF funding for treatment, but the board discussed continuing baseline engineering/survey work for a Keyes-to-Lancaster transmission main, comparing costs to other towns' treatment plants.
Revenue from bulk water sales is folded into the roughly stated operating budget; any surplus beyond covering the budget is used for capital items like equipment purchases.

budget_items.topic: New display TV for AMI meter monitoring
budget_items.what_was_said: The district purchased a large TV, described as inexpensive, to display real-time meter/leak data for staff and the public.

transfers.description: Materials purchase for Metal Lane water main project paid from the equipment and main account

decisions.decision: Proceed with switching accounting/billing software to the new vendor effective July 1st for accounting, with the resident billing switch possibly delayed to October or January depending on readiness.
Run the new billing system in parallel (dry run) alongside the existing NDS system before fully switching over, to check accuracy before sending bills.
Superintendent Fran will speak with a newspaper reporter (from the Ledger) about the sale of water to commercial buyers.
Hold off on any action regarding the zone one easement/kayak issue until the next meeting, pending the chair's input and a possible different approach than sending another letter to legal.
Test each of the four wells feeding the Lancaster source individually for PFAS to determine if a weaker well could be shut off while blending the others.
Cancel the July 8th and July 22nd commissioners' meetings and hold a single meeting on July 15th at 4:00, with a public notice of the schedule change.

Clerk will respond to a resident's inquiry by naming the district's attorney (KP Law, Brian Riley) but direct him to route further questions through the water district rather than contacting counsel directly, and will notify the attorney to confirm with the board before engaging.

minutes.headline: Commissioners rescinded their prior vote and will proceed with the new billing/accounting software vendor.
minutes.summary: The Water District Commissioners reversed a prior vote to cancel a new billing/accounting software switch, approved several purchases (pipe, materials, hydrants) for a PVC water main replacement on Metal Lane, and discussed ongoing PFAS treatment planning that remains stalled pending state guidance. They also tabled a legal/easement dispute over kayaks stored near the Hickory Hills wellfield, discussed the revenue benefits of selling water to commercial buyers, and set a revised July meeting schedule.

what_happened.line: Commissioners rescinded their June 10th vote and will proceed with the new billing/accounting software vendor.
They approved pipe, materials and hydrant purchases for the Metal Lane PVC water main replacement.
PFAS/PAS treatment planning stayed stalled, awaiting MassDEP guidance after voters denied SRF funding.
A legal dispute over kayaks stored near the Hickory Hills wellfield easement was tabled to the next meeting.
July's meeting schedule was consolidated to a single session on July 15th.

why_it_matters: The software switch changes how the district handles accounts starting July 1, with the resident billing cutover possibly landing in October or January depending on testing.
The Metal Lane purchases are capital spending from the equipment and main account, part of an ongoing water main replacement program.
PFAS treatment remains unresolved after voters turned down state loan funding, meaning future costs and any rate impact are still undetermined pending state guidance.
